trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether any credible IPO/S-1 or restructuring headline accompanies the odds move; if none, treat as noise. Watch MSFT tick vs QQQ to isolate idiosyncratic move.
time_plan.1h: Compare MSFT relative performance to Nasdaq-100 and to other AI-exposed names (NVDA); confirm whether move is OpenAI-specific or sector-wide.
time_plan.2h: Look for confirmation from wire services (Bloomberg/Reuters/CNBC) on OpenAI corporate-structure news; reassess direction if a concrete monetization vs dilution narrative emerges.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate whether the prediction-market move persisted or reverted; if reverted, close thesis as noise.
time_plan.12h: Mark realized MSFT return vs Nasdaq-100 beta-adjusted benchmark; log whether any public confirmation validated the leak hypothesis.

predictions.reasoning: Microsoft holds a large economic stake in OpenAI's for-profit entity, so it is the most direct listed proxy for OpenAI value-realization events. A sharp rise in IPO odds could imply an eventual mark-to-market/monetization of that stake (mildly positive) or signal structural changes to the Microsoft-OpenAI relationship and dilution of preferential access (mildly negative). The net sign is genuinely ambiguous, and MSFT is a ~$3T mega-cap where OpenAI IPO timing is a tiny fraction of the valuation — so any 12h move attributable to this signal is small and easily swamped by rates, mega-cap tech flow, and broad market beta.

evidence_used: OpenAI is privately held with no directly tradable equity, so implications must route through a proxy
Microsoft is the largest strategic/economic backer of OpenAI's for-profit arm
Market resolves on an IPO completion by end-2026, a long-dated corporate-action question
Description notes acquisition by a public company resolves 'No', reinforcing structural uncertainty
uncertainty_notes: No pure-play liquid instrument tracks OpenAI equity, making every proxy weak
Sign of the MSFT effect is ambiguous — monetization upside vs relationship/dilution downside
A 12h window is far too short for a 2026-dated IPO probability shift to produce a large, identifiable asset move
700bps threshold is implausible for a mega-cap over 12h from this catalyst

llm_justification.summary: OpenAI has no directly tradable stock, so the only reasonable public-market linkage runs through Microsoft as its largest backer, with weaker second-order links to AI-theme names and semis. But the sign is ambiguous (monetization upside vs dilution/relationship-change downside), the catalyst is long-dated to end-2026, and MSFT is a multi-trillion-dollar name where this is a marginal input. The mapping is weak; expected 12h moves are small and well below the 700bps tradable bar. Best treated as an 'unclear', low-confidence, non-tradable signal.
key_assumptions: Microsoft remains the primary listed vehicle exposed to OpenAI equity value
Prediction-market odds move is genuinely about IPO timing, not a data artifact
Broad tech-market beta dominates any OpenAI-specific idiosyncratic move over 12h
failure_modes: The odds move is noise or already-public information (e.g., recycled news), so no asset reaction
Direction is opposite to guess — an IPO could reduce Microsoft's preferential position, pressuring MSFT rather than lifting it
MSFT is a very weak proxy: OpenAI stake is small relative to Microsoft's total valuation, so the true beta is near zero
Move fully explained by macro/rates or mega-cap flow unrelated to OpenAI
No IPO-related public confirmation ever materializes, invalidating the leak premise
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
